split.selection_rules: Selection rules fixed before any outcome was read. LOOK-BACK: at share 0.99, over 14,21,24,28,30,60,90,180 days, the smallest grid look-back whose fitting-half target count equals the maximum; 'singled out' only if the previous grid point is at least 2 target days lower and the chosen is not the first grid point, else a range (grid points within 1 target day of the maximum). SHARE: at the chosen look-back, steps 0.999>0.995>0.99>0.95>0.90>0.80, yield = targets added / days added; a step is 'mostly targets' if yield > 0.5; chosen = the lower end of the last such step (none: 0.999); 'singled out' only if the step into it has yield >= 0.60 and the step out of it <= 0.40 (or none/zero days), else the range adds the neighbour whose adjacent step has yield in [0.40,0.60].

on_r29_flows.why: Control: the hold r28 build gives 410, and the same 410 days as the served table (0 days differ), though 988 held-row flows differ from the served table (served has a flow there, the hold build has none; value and return are identical on all 1,691,729 rows). Between hold r28 and hold r29: the flow differs on 47 account-days over 46 dates (42 zero to outflow, 2 outflow larger, 2 zero to inflow, 1 inflow to zero); 44 of the 47 change the outflow term the rule reads; value differs on 0; return differs on 2. Of the 44 outflow-changed account-days, 1 sits inside the 28-day window of a measured receipt day (inside the window of a day blanked under r29, of none blanked under r28); that one day, 2020-11-30, is the only day whose status changes: it is blanked under r29 flows and not under r28. With 24 days and 0.99 or 0.995 the same single day flips; with 24 days and 0.999 nothing changes (254 under both).

verdict_inputs: Fitted on half A alone (look-back 24 days singled out, share 0.99 not singled out: range 0.995 to 0.99) the rule blanked 72 of 77 target days and 0 of 4 other outlier days among 201 blanked on half B, and fitted on half B alone (look-back 24 not singled out, share 0.999 because no step added mostly targets) it blanked 37 of 85 target days (67 at 0.995) and 0 of 13 other outlier days among 128 on half A, against 76 of 85 and 72 of 77 with 28 days and 0.99 on the same halves (148 of 162 and 0 of 17 in all), so neither half chose round 69's constants, the halves chose the same look-back but not the same share, and the held-out target recall was 0.94 and 0.44 against 0.91 in all.

On the method_r29 build with the served hold list the rule blanks 411 days against 410 on the method_r28 build; 1 of the 44 days with a changed outflow sits in a window and it makes one day (2020-11-30) blank only under r29, no day is blank under r28 only, and the two days whose return changes are blanked under neither.

Of the 410 blanked days 163 carry a dividend, 108 a fee refund, 19 a reinvested distribution, 2 interest, 2 a 12b1 credit and 116 more than one class (mostly a dividend, interest and reinvested distribution with their cancels), 100 have an absolute return of 0.10 or less, 299 account-months lose at least one measured day and 10 lose every one (8 of them with a single measured day), and 63 account-months and 17 account-years with every day measured today would gain a blank day.
not_established: One hash partition was measured; the spread of held-out recall over other partitions is not established, and with 13 and 4 non-target outlier days in the two halves a count of 0 blanked is a thin test of the non-target side.
Both halves hold the same dates: 286 of the 410 blanked days are May-June 2026, so nothing was held out by time and a change of period is untested.
The classing of the 179 days (round 68) is taken as given and was not re-derived; 'target' is that classing's two causes.

The constants each half chose depend on the selection rules written before the run (smallest grid look-back at the target maximum; last step with yield above 0.5); other rules, or grid points between 21 and 24 days, would choose other constants. Half B's evidence picked 0.999 only because no step passed the 0.5 yield test.
The receipt-day flag was taken from the round-69 transaction match (effective row within 5 days of the trade date) and not re-derived; the r29 runs reuse the same flag for each (account, date).

Only one r29 build was run (at the served pin, with the hold list); the held rows' flows differ from the served table (988 account-days) without changing any blanked day. The served table itself carries r28 flows; no served table with r29 flows exists.
The count of flow-changed account-days is 47 by exact comparison, 44 of them in the outflow term the rule reads; the order and an earlier row say 44, and that figure was not otherwise reconciled.

Chain breaks are counted as blank rows in a calendar month or year on the table's own rows; no month or year return was recomputed, and the count depends on whether a row with no previous value (FIRST_DAY) is a blank (both are given).
Whether the 100 quiet blanked days (absolute return 0.10 or less) or the other blanked days outside the 179 are right to blank was not judged; no effect on any return was measured.

The class of receipt follows the order's grouping: the cancels DVX, INTX and DVRX are in the dividend, interest and reinvested classes, so a day with a receipt and its cancel is in 'more than one class'.
